# General CM compliance and a negative spectral moment

24 October 2026. Root derivation extending the scalar rank-one setting away
from exact optimality. This is a mathematical candidate for independent review,
not a novelty claim or an acquired physical device.

Use any connected positive finite internal spring graph, backbone mass m,
total mass M>m, side mass ms=M-m, one intercell spring K, and S=4K. Write

    D(q)=D0+s(q) vv^T, s(q)=4K sin^2(q/2),
    z=sqrt(masses)/sqrt(M), v=Mass^(-1/2)e_b,
    u=v-z/sqrt(M), w=-(M/ms)u.

The local relative internal CM coordinate Y has force vector w. In particular,
w is perpendicular to z. None of this assumes the optimal two-pole response.

## 1. Compliance is independent of Bloch wave number for every cell

For q!=0, let D(q)x=w. Taking the inner product with z gives
s(q)(z^T v)(v^T x)=0, hence v^T x=0. Therefore D0 x=w and

    x=D0^+ w+a z,
    w^T D(q)^(-1)w=w^T D0^+ w=:C_CM.

The translation-free q=0 inverse gives the same contraction. Thus Fourier
averaging proves the same local compliance on any finite periodic ring.
The harmonic Gibbs inequality gives Var(Y)>=k_B T C_CM. This remains a Gibbs
statement, not a general nonequilibrium variance assertion.

Let the positive visible spectral residues of D0 at r_j^2 be c_j. Then

    q(t)=v^T(D0+tI)^(-1)v=1/(Mt)+sum_j c_j/(t+r_j^2),
    tau=sum_j c_j/r_j^2=u^T D0^+u,
    C_CM=(M/ms)^2 tau.

This includes repeated visible frequencies after combining residues and all
dark modes after cancellation.

## 2. Exact negative-cubic spectral moment

For active squared band endpoints 0=alpha0<beta0<alpha1<...<betaL,

    R(t)=1+S q(t)=product_j(t+beta_j)/product_j(t+alpha_j).

Expanding log R as t decreases to zero gives

    log R(t)=log[S/(Mt)]+(M/S+M tau)t+O(t^2),
    sum_j 1/beta_j-sum_(j>=1)1/alpha_j=M/S+M tau.

Let chi be the active band indicator and Omega^2=S/M. Since chi and
1_[0,Omega] both equal one near zero, their difference is integrable against
omega^-3. Endpoint integration yields

    integral_0^infty [1_[0,Omega](omega)-chi(omega)]/omega^3 d omega
      = M tau/2
      = ms^2 C_CM/(2M).

Thus compliance is a THIRD exact moment constraint supplementing the trace
and logarithmic moment constraints. It is not confined to exact optimality.
Units agree: each side has units time^2; C_CM has units time^2/mass.

source_excerpts.text:
# Static relative compliance and the Bose-conductance limit

This audit treats a finite connected scalar cell with one backbone coordinate,
one intercell spring `K`, total mass `M`, backbone mass `m`, and side mass
`m_s=M-m>0`. In mass-normalized coordinates,

`D(s)=D0+s vv^T`, `s=4K sin^2(q/2)`, `v=e_b/sqrt(m)`,

where `D0` is positive semidefinite with the unique translation nullvector
`z=sqrt(mass)/sqrt(M)`. Set `u=v-z/sqrt(M)` and `w=-(M/m_s)u`. Then
`z^T v=1/sqrt(M)` and `u^Tz=0`.

## Exact compliance identity

For every `s>0`, `D(s)` is positive definite: a null vector would have to be
both a multiple of `z` and orthogonal to `v`, which is impossible unless it
is zero. Let `y=D(s)^(-1)u`. Multiplying `D(s)y=u` by `z^T` gives

`s(z^T v)(v^T y)=z^T u=0`,

so `v^T y=0` and therefore `D0 y=u`. The general solution is
`y=D0^+u+gamma z`. Since `v^TD0^+u=u^TD0^+u` and `v^Tz=1/sqrt(M)`,
the constraint `v^Ty=0` fixes `gamma=-sqrt(M) u^TD0^+u`. Thus

`u^T D(s)^(-1)u=u^TD0^+u`,

and the asserted identity follows exactly:

`w^T D(s)^(-1)w=(M/m_s)^2 u^TD0^+u`, for every `s>0`.

It is independent of wave number, not a small-`s` approximation. For a single
backbone-to-side spring of stiffness `k`, it reduces to the familiar
relative-coordinate compliance `1/k`.

## Endpoint formula and inverse-cubic spectral moment

Write the ordered endpoint eigenvalues as `alpha_0=0,alpha_1,...` for `D0`
and `beta_0,beta_1,...` for `D0+S vv^T`, where `S=4K`. Dark eigenvalues
cancel from all formulas below. With

`q(t)=v^T(D0+tI)^(-1)v`,

the translation-mode decomposition gives

`q(t)=1/(M t)+u^T(D0+tI)^(-1)u`,
`c:=u^TD0^+u=lim_(t down 0)[q(t)-1/(M t)]`.

The determinant lemma says

`prod_j(t+beta_j)/prod_j(t+alpha_j)=1+S q(t)`.

Expanding at zero and using
`prod_j beta_j/prod_(j>0)alpha_j=S/M` yields

`c = (1/M)[sum_j 1/beta_j - sum_(j>0)1/alpha_j] - 1/S`.

Thus the static compliance `C=w^TD(s)^(-1)w` is determined exactly by the
inverse-squared-frequency endpoint moment:

`C=(M/m_s)^2 c`.

There is an equivalent passband formula. Let
`Omega^2=S/M`,
`chi(omega)=sum_j 1_[sqrt(alpha_j),sqrt(beta_j)](omega)`, and
`chi_rig=1_[0,Omega]`. Then endpoint integration gives

`integral_0^infinity [chi(omega)-chi_rig(omega)]/omega^3 d omega`
`= (1/2)[sum_(j>0)1/alpha_j - sum_j1/beta_j + 1/Omega^2]`
`= -M c/2 = -m_s^2 C/(2M)`.
